title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 25-26
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 25 to 26 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 25 to 26 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 25 to 26.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 25 to 26** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः । अहः संवर्तको वह्निरनिलो धरणीधरः ॥** **सुप्रसादः प्रसन्नात्मा विश्वधृग्विश्वभुग्विभुः । सत्कर्ता सत्कृतः साधुर्जह्नुर्नारायणो नरः ॥**

He turns the wheel of the world, he never returns to ignorance, he covers all and crushes his foes. Day, the fire of dissolution and the wind are that God of gods. He holds up the earth. He is full of grace, and his mind is at peace. The one who holds and enjoys the universe is that God of gods. He honours and is honoured, the saint, Narayana and Nara.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 25 to 26 mean?
faq.a: He turns the wheel of the world, he never returns to ignorance, he covers all and crushes his foes. Day, the fire of dissolution and the wind are that God of gods. He holds up the earth. He is full of grace, and his mind is at peace. The one who holds and enjoys the universe is that God of gods. He honours and is honoured, the saint, Narayana and Nara.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
